lines.text: Total votes = valid votes + invalid or blank votes.

candidates.question:
A class records five variables: the time to run 100 m, the number of goals scored in a match, the mass of a parcel, eye colour, and shoe size.
How many of these variables are numerical continuous?

lines.text: Numerical continuous data is measured and can take any value in a range.
Time to run 100 m: continuous. Mass of a parcel: continuous.
Number of goals and shoe size: numerical discrete. Eye colour: categorical.

skill.title: Describe a distribution's shape
skill.output: symmetric, positive/negative skew; effect on mean vs median

candidates.question:
The number of goals scored by ten teams in a season is shown in a stem-and-leaf plot. The values are:
$2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 6, 8, 15, 30$
The plot has a long tail on the right, so the distribution is positively skewed. Find the mean minus the median.

lines.text: The mean is greater than the median, as expected for a positive skew.

candidates.question:
Ten students' marks in a test are:
$10, 45, 60, 62, 64, 65, 66, 68, 70, 70$
The histogram has a long tail on the left, so the distribution is negatively skewed. Find the median minus the mean.

lines.text: The median is greater than the mean, as expected for a negative skew.

candidates.question:
Eleven students recorded the hours they spent online in a week:
$4, 5, 6, 6, 7, 7, 7, 8, 8, 9, 10$
The dot plot is symmetric about the middle value. Find the mean minus the median.

lines.text: There are 11 values, so the median is the 6th value.
The mean equals the median, as expected for a symmetric distribution.

skill.title: Explain the effect of outliers on summary statistics

steps.title: Say how the mean is affected

lines.text: Making the biggest number bigger increases the total (sum) of the 10 numbers.
The mean is the total divided by 10, so the mean increases as well.

steps.title: Say how the median is affected

lines.text: For 10 numbers the median depends only on the middle two values, the 5th and 6th biggest.
The biggest number is the 10th, so changing it does not change the 5th or 6th values. The median stays the same.
Tick the box for the mean only.

candidates.question:
Five numbers are $10, 12, 14, 16, 18$. The largest number, 18, is replaced by 38.
Find how much the mean increases by, and say whether the median changes.

steps.title: Find the original and new means

lines.text: The median is the middle value, 14, before and after. The median does not change.

candidates.question:
The data set $6, 7, 8, 9, 60$ contains an outlier, 60.
Find how much the mean decreases by when 60 is removed.

steps.title: Find the mean with the outlier

lines.text: The median only moves from 8 to 7.5, so the outlier affects the mean far more.

candidates.question:
The number of text messages sent by ten students in one day was:
$12, 14, 15, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 52$
An outlier is a value more than $1.5 \times IQR$ above $Q_3$ or below $Q_1$.
Find the upper limit above which a value is an outlier.

lines.text: The lower half is $12, 14, 15, 15, 16$, so $Q_1 = 15$.
The upper half is $17, 18, 19, 20, 52$, so $Q_3 = 19$.
$52 > 25$, so 52 is an outlier.

candidates.question:
The ages of ten members of a club are:
$3, 41, 43, 44, 46, 47, 49, 50, 52, 90$
An outlier is a value more than $1.5 \times IQR$ above $Q_3$ or below $Q_1$.
Find the value below which an age would be an outlier.

lines.text: The lower half is $3, 41, 43, 44, 46$, so $Q_1 = 43$.
The upper half is $47, 49, 50, 52, 90$, so $Q_3 = 50$.
$3 < 32.5$, so the age 3 is an outlier.

candidates.question:
Nine houses on a road have these numbers of residents:
$6, 8, 9, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14$
An outlier is a value more than $1.5 \times IQR$ above $Q_3$ or below $Q_1$.
Using the quartiles of these nine values, find the smallest whole number of residents that would be an outlier above the data.

lines.text: Leave out the median, 10. The lower half is $6, 8, 9, 9$, so $Q_1 = 8.5$.
The upper half is $11, 12, 13, 14$, so $Q_3 = 12.5$.
A value must be more than 18.5, so the smallest whole number is 19.

candidates.question:
In a test taken by 50 students, Aoife scored more marks than 36 of the other students.
Find Aoife's percentile rank.

lines.text: The percentile rank is the percentage of students who scored below Aoife.
Aoife is at the 72nd percentile.

candidates.question:
A student's mark in a national exam is at the 85th percentile. 40 students sat the exam.
How many students scored lower than this student?

lines.text: The 85th percentile means 85% of the students scored lower.

candidates.question:
The times, in minutes, taken by 12 runners to finish a race are:
$3,\ 4,\ 6,\ 7,\ 8,\ 9,\ 10,\ 12,\ 14,\ 16,\ 18,\ 20$
Find the 75th percentile of the times.

steps.title: Link the percentile to a quartile

lines.text: The 75th percentile is the upper quartile $Q_3$.

steps.title: Find the upper half of the data

lines.text: There are 12 values, so the upper half is the 6 largest: $10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20$.
